stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +22.1%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $140.75 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 148 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 148 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-25.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-12) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Airplane Turbulence Is Extremely Hard to Predict, but Maybe Not for Long
stories.excerpt: The “hardest remaining problem in classical physics” gets a boost from terabytes of crowdsourced data and new ways of using machine learning and AI.
stories.lead:
In the early 1500s, an Italian polymath named Leonardo da Vinci took a good crack at exactly the phenomenon that makes nervous fliers clutch their airplane seats in fear and flight attendants push their carts back to the galleys with haste: turbulence.

Da Vinci was fascinated by swirling, chaotic eddies of water, movements so complex that he made hundreds of drawings of his observations. Why, exactly, did water—any fluid, really, be it atmospheric air or blood in the heart—move in that way?

stories.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
stories.excerpt: Frontier AI is already solving problems that once took top physicists a full day.
stories.lead: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics.

stories.title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
stories.excerpt: A new test assumes AI agents can go rogue—and asks whether they can resist temptation.
stories.lead:
Leather-clad billionaires aren’t the only ones who can be led astray by alleged honeypots.

Researchers at Anthropic have developed Siren, a new honeypot test for artificial intelligence agents. The setup puts agents in realistic simulations designed to tempt them into misbehaving. How they respond will help researchers evaluate the likelihood that new models will go rogue when deployed in the real world, as well as the effectiveness of different safety measures.

stories.title: New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause
stories.excerpt: Text of the treaties will be published this afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.
stories.lead:
The government and the EU are set to publish the texts of two treaties that were agreed last week as part of a post-Brexit reset.

The BBC understands the deal covering food exports has a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party ended the agreement, they would have to pay to rebuild border checks infrastructure, which will be significantly scaled back as part of the new deal.

stories.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
stories.excerpt: The Trump administration gave Elon Musk's SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a move that has raised skepticism among scientists.
stories.lead: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission lauded its authorization as a historic first amid the artificial intelligence race. It said that SpaceX's one million "orbital compute modules" (forming a data center constellation called "Starmind") would process massive amounts of data that would be used back on Earth — and bring humans closer to harnessing "the full power of the sun."

stories.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
stories.excerpt: Taylor revealed his battle with Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2022. He was the guitarist of the 1980s English band Duran Duran, whose pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Rio".
stories.lead:
Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

stories.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats

Nearly a third of small-boat crossings to the UK, in the first four months of 2026, allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

stories.title: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
stories.excerpt: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.
stories.lead:
A federal judge has blocked President Trump and his administration from taking action to challenge the ABC television network's broadcast licenses, finding it to be an unconstitutional punishment for satire, commentary and news coverage that Trump doesn't like.

In her preliminary injunction filed Wednesday, U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan found that the federal agency's early reviews represented retaliation for speech the Trump administration resented.

Such perceived offenses included late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's jabs at the president, the critical remarks of hosts on the chat show The View, and the moderation of a presidential debate in September 2024.

stories.title: Car finance compensation payments explained
stories.excerpt: Millions could be entitled to compensation as a result of commission arrangements between lenders and dealers.
stories.lead:
The vast majority of new cars, and many second-hand ones, are bought with finance agreements. Customers pay an initial deposit to secure the vehicle, then a monthly fee with interest.

Compensation could be given to many of those who took out a car loan between April 2007 and November 2024.

The decision by the FCA, the financial regulator, applies to about 12 million car loans - about 37% of the total number during the period.

Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy.

Nvidia has halted chip shipments to south-east Asia, as the sell-off in stock markets eased.

The US chipmaker, which is at the heart of the AI boom, has told manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to the Financial Times, citing three unnamed sources.

stories.title: Parents cutting basics at Christmas, charity warns
stories.excerpt: The chief executive of Worthing Soup Kitchen says some families choose between food and presents.
stories.lead:
Christmas is likely to see families cut back on essentials to try and meet the expenses of the festive period, a West Sussex soup kitchen has warned.

Katrina McCormack, chief executive of the Shout Worthing Soup Kitchen, told BBC Radio Sussex that they are forced to limit the amount of support they can give due to high demand at Christmas, and make sure their shelves are stocked.

It comes at the start of a campaign to raise thousands for turkey and other Christmas trimmings for struggling families, which the charity says is a "driving force" for their work in December.
